---- MODULE W4Od11m4p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences
CONSTANTS Jobs, Slots, MaxQueue, MaxOverride
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES waiting, held, owner, done, overrides
vars == <<waiting, held, owner, done, overrides>>

InQueue(j) == \E i \in 1..Len(waiting) : waiting[i] = j

Init ==
    /\ waiting = << >>
    /\ held = [j \in Jobs |-> NONE]
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ done = {}
    /\ overrides = 0

Submit(j) ==
    /\ held[j] = NONE
    /\ ~InQueue(j)
    /\ Len(waiting) < MaxQueue
    /\ waiting' = Append(waiting, j)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<held, owner, done, overrides>>

Assign ==
    /\ waiting # << >>
    /\ \E s \in Slots :
        /\ owner[s] = NONE
        /\ LET h == Head(waiting) IN
            /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![h] = s]
            /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = h]
            /\ waiting' = Tail(waiting)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<done, overrides>>

Complete(j) ==
    /\ held[j] # NONE
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![held[j]] = NONE]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![j] = NONE]
    /\ done' = done \cup {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, overrides>>

AdminEvict(j) ==
    /\ overrides < MaxOverride
    /\ held[j] # NONE
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![held[j]] = NONE]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![j] = NONE]
    /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, done>>

Next ==
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Submit(j)
    \/ Assign
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Complete(j)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : AdminEvict(j)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OwnershipConsistent ==
    /\ \A j \in Jobs : held[j] # NONE => owner[held[j]] = j
    /\ \A s \in Slots : owner[s] # NONE => held[owner[s]] = s
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Jobs = {j1, j2, j3} Slots = {s1, s2} MaxQueue = 2 MaxOverride = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OwnershipConsistent
nl:
A print shop runs a spooler that feeds print jobs into a small set of physical output slots. Incoming jobs first land in a bounded waiting queue; when the queue is already full the spooler applies backpressure and refuses to accept the job. The spooler keeps two independent records of slot usage: for each job it records which slot that job currently holds, and for each slot it records which job currently owns it. When a waiting job is assigned, the spooler picks a slot whose owner record is empty, writes the slot into the job's record and the job into the slot's record, and removes the job from the queue. When a job completes, both records for that job and its slot are cleared. A privileged administrator may forcibly evict a job from its slot, clearing both records, but only a bounded number of such overrides are allowed. The two records must always agree with each other so that a slot is never quietly handed to two different jobs.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the per-job and per-slot ownership records are always mutually consistent, so no slot is ever recorded as owned by one job while a different job believes it holds that slot.

---- MODULE W4Od17m9p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Carousels, MaxEpoch, CapMax

VARIABLES epoch, load, cap, pool, delivered
vars == <<epoch, load, cap, pool, delivered>>

Msgs == [car : Carousels, ep : 0..MaxEpoch]

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ load = [c \in Carousels |-> 0]
    /\ cap = [c \in Carousels |-> 1]
    /\ pool = {}
    /\ delivered = {}

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ \E newcap \in [Carousels -> 1..CapMax] :
        /\ \A c \in Carousels : newcap[c] >= load[c]
        /\ cap' = newcap
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, pool, delivered>>

Issue(c) ==
    /\ [car |-> c, ep |-> epoch] \notin pool
    /\ pool' = pool \cup {[car |-> c, ep |-> epoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, load, cap, delivered>>

Deliver ==
    /\ \E m \in pool :
        /\ m.ep = epoch
        /\ load[m.car] < cap[m.car]
        /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![m.car] = @ + 1]
        /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
        /\ delivered' = delivered \cup {m.car}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap>>

DropStale ==
    /\ \E m \in pool :
        /\ m.ep < epoch
        /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, load, cap, delivered>>

Collect(c) ==
    /\ load[c] > 0
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![c] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap, pool, delivered>>

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E c \in Carousels : Issue(c)
    \/ Deliver
    \/ DropStale
    \/ \E c \in Carousels : Collect(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

WithinCapacity == \A c \in Carousels : load[c] <= cap[c]
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Carousels = {c1, c2} MaxEpoch = 2 CapMax = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT WithinCapacity
nl:
An airport baggage router directs bags onto a set of carousels. A central controller occasionally performs a numbered reconfiguration: it bumps a configuration epoch and, at the same time, chooses new per-carousel capacity limits, but it is never allowed to set a carousel's capacity below the number of bags already sitting on it. Routing commands are issued as messages stamped with the epoch that was current when they were created, and these messages float in a shared pool from which they may be acted on in any order, not first-in-first-out. A delivery message is honoured only if its epoch still matches the current configuration epoch and the target carousel has room; acting on it places one more bag on that carousel. A message whose epoch is older than the current epoch is stale and is simply discarded. Bags are also continuously removed from carousels as travellers collect them. The router must guarantee that no carousel ever holds more bags than its current capacity permits.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every carousel's bag count is always less than or equal to its current configured capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od17m3p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Nodes, MaxTerm
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES leader, term, crashed, finalizedTerms
vars == <<leader, term, crashed, finalizedTerms>>

Init ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ term = 0
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ finalizedTerms = {}

Elect(n) ==
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ (leader = NONE \/ leader \in crashed)
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, finalizedTerms>>

Crash(n) ==
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ Cardinality(crashed) < Cardinality(Nodes) - 1
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {n}
    /\ leader' = IF leader = n THEN NONE ELSE leader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, finalizedTerms>>

Restart(n) ==
    /\ n \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, finalizedTerms>>

Finalize(n) ==
    /\ leader = n
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ finalizedTerms = {}
    /\ finalizedTerms' = {term}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Crash(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Restart(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Finalize(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

UniqueFinalize == \A a, b \in finalizedTerms : a = b
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Nodes = {n1, n2, n3} MaxTerm = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT UniqueFinalize
nl:
An airport baggage router is coordinated by a small cluster of controller nodes that elect a leader. Each election starts a new numbered term, and a node may only become leader when there is currently no working leader. Any node may crash silently at any time; a crash is not announced, it simply removes the node from service, and if the crashed node was the leader the leadership becomes vacant, prompting a failover election in a later term. To keep at least one controller available the system never lets every node crash. A crashed node may later restart and rejoin. The single irreversible action in this system is finalizing the day's dispatch plan, which physically commits bags to their destinations and cannot be undone. Only the current working leader may finalize, and the design intends that finalization happen at most once across the entire run, recorded together with the term in which it occurred. Because a naive implementation could finalize again after a failover, the safety requirement is that finalization never occurs in two different terms.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the set of terms in which the dispatch plan was finalized never contains two distinct terms, so the irreversible finalize action happens in at most one term.

---- MODULE W4Od15m7p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Instances, PoolCap, MaxReserve

VARIABLES poolUsed, view, pending, matched
vars == <<poolUsed, view, pending, matched>>

Init ==
    /\ poolUsed = 0
    /\ view = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
    /\ pending = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
    /\ matched = [i \in Instances |-> 0]

Read(i) ==
    /\ pending[i] = 0
    /\ view' = [view EXCEPT ![i] = poolUsed]
    /\ \E k \in 1..MaxReserve : pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![i] = k]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<poolUsed, matched>>

CasSucceed(i) ==
    /\ pending[i] > 0
    /\ view[i] = poolUsed
    /\ poolUsed + pending[i] <= PoolCap
    /\ poolUsed' = poolUsed + pending[i]
    /\ matched' = [matched EXCEPT ![i] = @ + pending[i]]
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED view

CasStale(i) ==
    /\ pending[i] > 0
    /\ view[i] # poolUsed
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<poolUsed, view, matched>>

CasOverflow(i) ==
    /\ pending[i] > 0
    /\ view[i] = poolUsed
    /\ poolUsed + pending[i] > PoolCap
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<poolUsed, view, matched>>

Settle(i) ==
    /\ matched[i] > 0
    /\ matched' = [matched EXCEPT ![i] = @ - 1]
    /\ poolUsed' = poolUsed - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<view, pending>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Read(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : CasSucceed(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : CasStale(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : CasOverflow(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Settle(i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

PoolWithinCapacity == poolUsed <= PoolCap
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Instances = {a, b} PoolCap = 3 MaxReserve = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT PoolWithinCapacity
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction in which two independent matching instances draw share liquidity from one shared pool. The pool's usage is held in a single register that both instances update using a compare-and-swap discipline. To reserve liquidity, an instance first takes a private snapshot of the shared register and decides how many units it wants to reserve. It then attempts a compare-and-swap: the swap succeeds only if the register still equals the snapshot and the resulting total would not exceed the pool's fixed capacity; on success the register advances and the instance credits the units to its matched volume. If the register has moved since the snapshot, the swap fails as stale and the instance abandons that attempt to retry later. If the snapshot is current but the reservation would overflow capacity, the attempt is abandoned as well. Settlement can later release matched units, decrementing both the instance's matched volume and the shared register. Because the two instances race on the same register, the invariant is that the shared usage register never exceeds the pool capacity.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared pool-usage register is always less than or equal to the fixed pool capacity, even though two instances update it concurrently.

---- MODULE W4Od9m5p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Nodes, Proposals, Quorum
NONE == -1
DELTA == [p \in Proposals |-> p]

RECURSIVE SumDelta(_)
SumDelta(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE e \in S : TRUE IN DELTA[x] + SumDelta(S \ {x})

VARIABLES total, committed, snap, base, votes
vars == <<total, committed, snap, base, votes>>

Init ==
    /\ total = 0
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ snap = [p \in Proposals |-> NONE]
    /\ base = [p \in Proposals |-> {}]
    /\ votes = [p \in Proposals |-> {}]

Start(p) ==
    /\ snap[p] = NONE
    /\ p \notin committed
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![p] = total]
    /\ base' = [base EXCEPT ![p] = committed]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<total, committed>>

Vote(n, p) ==
    /\ snap[p] # NONE
    /\ p \notin committed
    /\ n \notin votes[p]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = @ \cup {n}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<total, committed, snap, base>>

Commit(p) ==
    /\ snap[p] # NONE
    /\ p \notin committed
    /\ Cardinality(votes[p]) >= Quorum
    /\ base[p] = committed
    /\ total' = snap[p] + DELTA[p]
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {p}
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![p] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<base, votes>>

Abort(p) ==
    /\ snap[p] # NONE
    /\ p \notin committed
    /\ base[p] # committed
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![p] = NONE]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<total, committed, base>>

Recover(p) ==
    /\ p \in committed
    /\ committed' = committed \ {p}
    /\ total' = total - DELTA[p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, base, votes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Proposals : Start(p)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, p \in Proposals : Vote(n, p)
    \/ \E p \in Proposals : Commit(p)
    \/ \E p \in Proposals : Abort(p)
    \/ \E p \in Proposals : Recover(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate == total = SumDelta(committed)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Nodes = {n1, n2, n3} Proposals = {1, 2} Quorum = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A power-grid load shedder coordinates how much load to shed through a shared record holding the current total shed amount. Several controller nodes vote on shedding proposals, and a proposal may only be committed once a quorum of nodes has voted for it. Each proposal, when it starts, takes a private snapshot of the current total and also snapshots the set of already-committed proposals. Nodes then cast their votes over time; a node may be slow, casting its vote late, but it is never considered failed, so every node can eventually vote. Committing a proposal performs a read-modify-write: it writes the snapshotted total plus the proposal's fixed shed delta back into the shared total. To avoid a lost update, a commit is only allowed if the committed-set has not changed since the proposal took its snapshot; if it has changed, the proposal aborts and retries. Committed load can later be recovered, which removes the proposal from the committed set and subtracts its delta. The shared total must always equal the sum of the shed deltas of exactly the currently committed proposals.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared total shed amount always equals the sum of the shed deltas of the currently committed proposals, so no committed update is ever lost or double-counted.

---- MODULE W4Od3m1p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Slots, N
NONE == -1
Banks == 0..(N-1)

VARIABLES holder, pending, processed, owner, crashed
vars == <<holder, pending, processed, owner, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ holder = 0
    /\ pending = Slots
    /\ processed = {}
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ crashed = {}

PassToken ==
    /\ holder \notin crashed
    /\ LET succ == CHOOSE k \in 1..N : ((holder + k) % N) \notin crashed
       IN holder' = (holder + succ) % N
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, processed, owner, crashed>>

Claim(s) ==
    /\ holder \notin crashed
    /\ s \in pending
    /\ pending' = pending \ {s}
    /\ processed' = processed \cup {s}
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = holder]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, crashed>>

Crash(b) ==
    /\ b \notin crashed
    /\ Cardinality(crashed) < N - 1
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {b}
    /\ holder' = IF b = holder
                 THEN CHOOSE c \in Banks : c \notin (crashed \cup {b})
                 ELSE holder
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, processed, owner>>

Restart(b) ==
    /\ b \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, pending, processed, owner>>

Recycle ==
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ pending' = processed
    /\ processed' = {}
    /\ owner' = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Claim(s)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Crash(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Restart(b)
    \/ Recycle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
    /\ pending \cap processed = {}
    /\ \A s \in Slots : owner[s] # NONE => s \in processed
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Slots = {sa, sb} N = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A group of banks settle an interbank batch by circulating a single token around a ring. Only the bank currently holding the token may process settlement slots, giving it exclusive access. The batch begins with every slot pending and none processed. When the token holder processes a slot, that slot moves from the pending set into the processed set and is stamped with the owning bank. The token is passed to the next still-alive bank around the ring. A bank may crash silently at any time, without warning; the system keeps at least one bank alive, and if the crashing bank was holding the token the token is handed to some surviving bank. A crashed bank may later restart and rejoin the ring. Once every slot has been processed, the batch recycles: the processed slots become pending again for the next batch and ownership stamps are cleared. The core requirement is that a slot is never simultaneously pending and processed, so no settlement slot is ever allocated or handled twice at the same time.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the pending and processed slot sets are always disjoint and every owned slot is in the processed set, so no slot is double-allocated.

---- MODULE W4Od9m8p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences
CONSTANTS Feeders, Regions, Procs, MaxOverride
NONE == "none"
FeederRegion(f) == f % 2
Range(s) == {s[i] : i \in 1..Len(s)}

VARIABLES coarse, fine, tripLog, overrides
vars == <<coarse, fine, tripLog, overrides>>

Init ==
    /\ coarse = [r \in Regions |-> NONE]
    /\ fine = [f \in Feeders |-> NONE]
    /\ tripLog = << >>
    /\ overrides = 0

AcquireCoarse(p, r) ==
    /\ coarse[r] = NONE
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![r] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, tripLog, overrides>>

ReleaseCoarse(p, r) ==
    /\ coarse[r] = p
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, tripLog, overrides>>

AcquireFine(p, f) ==
    /\ coarse[FeederRegion(f)] = p
    /\ fine[f] = NONE
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![f] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, tripLog, overrides>>

ReleaseFine(p, f) ==
    /\ fine[f] = p
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![f] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, tripLog, overrides>>

Trip(p, f) ==
    /\ fine[f] = p
    /\ coarse[FeederRegion(f)] = p
    /\ f \notin Range(tripLog)
    /\ tripLog' = Append(tripLog, f)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, overrides>>

AdminOverride(f) ==
    /\ overrides < MaxOverride
    /\ f \notin Range(tripLog)
    /\ tripLog' = Append(tripLog, f)
    /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Procs, r \in Regions : AcquireCoarse(p, r)
    \/ \E p \in Procs, r \in Regions : ReleaseCoarse(p, r)
    \/ \E p \in Procs, f \in Feeders : AcquireFine(p, f)
    \/ \E p \in Procs, f \in Feeders : ReleaseFine(p, f)
    \/ \E p \in Procs, f \in Feeders : Trip(p, f)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : AdminOverride(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoRetrip == \A i, j \in 1..Len(tripLog) : tripLog[i] = tripLog[j] => i = j
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Feeders = {1, 2, 3} Regions = {0, 1} Procs = {p1, p2} MaxOverride = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoRetrip
nl:
A power-grid load shedder protects feeders using a two-level, coarse-then-fine locking discipline. Each feeder belongs to a region; the whole region is a coarse lock and each individual feeder is a fine lock. A shedding process must first acquire the coarse lock on a feeder's region, and only then may it acquire the fine lock on that specific feeder. Tripping a feeder's breaker is the one irreversible action in the system: once a feeder has been tripped it is permanently recorded and must never be tripped a second time. A process may trip a feeder only while it holds both the region's coarse lock and the feeder's own fine lock, and only if that feeder has not already been tripped. Locks may be released and re-acquired freely. A privileged administrator override may also trip a feeder directly, bypassing the lock hierarchy, but the override is bounded in number and it too refuses to re-trip an already-tripped feeder. All trip events are recorded in an append-only log.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the trip log never records the same feeder twice, so the irreversible trip action happens at most once per feeder.

---- MODULE W4Od6m5p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Participants, Quorum, MaxEpoch
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES epoch, members, pool, dispatcher, dispEpoch
vars == <<epoch, members, pool, dispatcher, dispEpoch>>

Votes(c) == {m \in pool : m.cand = c /\ m.voter \in members}

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ members = Participants
    /\ pool = {}
    /\ dispatcher = NONE
    /\ dispEpoch = -1

CastVote(v, c) ==
    /\ v \in members
    /\ [voter |-> v, cand |-> c] \notin pool
    /\ pool' = pool \cup {[voter |-> v, cand |-> c]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, members, dispatcher, dispEpoch>>

Install(c) ==
    /\ c \in members
    /\ Cardinality(Votes(c)) >= Quorum
    /\ dispatcher' = c
    /\ dispEpoch' = epoch
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, members, pool>>

StepDown ==
    /\ dispatcher # NONE
    /\ dispatcher' = NONE
    /\ dispEpoch' = -1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, members, pool>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ pool' = {}
    /\ dispatcher' = NONE
    /\ dispEpoch' = -1
    /\ UNCHANGED members

AddMember(m) ==
    /\ m \notin members
    /\ members' = members \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, pool, dispatcher, dispEpoch>>

RemoveMember(m) ==
    /\ m \in members
    /\ Cardinality(members) > Quorum
    /\ members' = members \ {m}
    /\ dispatcher' = IF dispatcher = m THEN NONE ELSE dispatcher
    /\ dispEpoch' = IF dispatcher = m THEN -1 ELSE dispEpoch
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, pool>>

Next ==
    \/ \E v \in Participants, c \in Participants : CastVote(v, c)
    \/ \E c \in Participants : Install(c)
    \/ StepDown
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E m \in Participants : AddMember(m)
    \/ \E m \in Participants : RemoveMember(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AuthorizedDispatcher ==
    dispatcher = NONE \/ (dispatcher \in members /\ dispEpoch = epoch)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Participants = {a, b, c} Quorum = 2 MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AuthorizedDispatcher
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper is coordinated by a set of controller participants that vote to install a dispatcher who is allowed to direct the cars. The current authorized membership can change as controllers join or leave, and a configuration epoch is bumped whenever the system is reconfigured. Controllers cast votes for a candidate dispatcher; votes sit in a shared pool and may be counted in any order, not in the order they were cast. A candidate is installed as dispatcher only when a quorum of votes from currently authorized members backs it and the candidate is itself an authorized member, and the installation is stamped with the current epoch. Whenever the system reconfigures to a new epoch, the whole vote pool is discarded and any sitting dispatcher is cleared, because its authorization is now stale. If the sitting dispatcher is removed from the membership, it is likewise cleared. The requirement is that any sitting dispatcher is always a currently authorized member whose installation epoch matches the current epoch, so no stale or unauthorized participant ever holds the dispatch privilege.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a dispatcher is installed, that dispatcher is a current authorized member and its installation epoch equals the current epoch.

---- MODULE W4Od10m8p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Trains, Lines, Blocks
NONE == -1
BlockLine(b) == b % 2

VARIABLES lineLock, blockOcc, holdingLine, holdingBlock, crashed
vars == <<lineLock, blockOcc, holdingLine, holdingBlock, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ lineLock = [l \in Lines |-> NONE]
    /\ blockOcc = [b \in Blocks |-> NONE]
    /\ holdingLine = [t \in Trains |-> NONE]
    /\ holdingBlock = [t \in Trains |-> NONE]
    /\ crashed = {}

AcquireLine(t, l) ==
    /\ t \notin crashed
    /\ holdingLine[t] = NONE
    /\ lineLock[l] = NONE
    /\ lineLock' = [lineLock EXCEPT ![l] = t]
    /\ holdingLine' = [holdingLine EXCEPT ![t] = l]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<blockOcc, holdingBlock, crashed>>

EnterBlock(t, b) ==
    /\ t \notin crashed
    /\ holdingLine[t] = BlockLine(b)
    /\ holdingBlock[t] = NONE
    /\ blockOcc[b] = NONE
    /\ blockOcc' = [blockOcc EXCEPT ![b] = t]
    /\ holdingBlock' = [holdingBlock EXCEPT ![t] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lineLock, holdingLine, crashed>>

LeaveBlock(t) ==
    /\ holdingBlock[t] # NONE
    /\ blockOcc' = [blockOcc EXCEPT ![holdingBlock[t]] = NONE]
    /\ holdingBlock' = [holdingBlock EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lineLock, holdingLine, crashed>>

ReleaseLine(t) ==
    /\ holdingLine[t] # NONE
    /\ holdingBlock[t] = NONE
    /\ lineLock' = [lineLock EXCEPT ![holdingLine[t]] = NONE]
    /\ holdingLine' = [holdingLine EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<blockOcc, holdingBlock, crashed>>

Crash(t) ==
    /\ t \notin crashed
    /\ Cardinality(crashed) < Cardinality(Trains) - 1
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {t}
    /\ lineLock' = [l \in Lines |-> IF lineLock[l] = t THEN NONE ELSE lineLock[l]]
    /\ blockOcc' = [b \in Blocks |-> IF blockOcc[b] = t THEN NONE ELSE blockOcc[b]]
    /\ holdingLine' = [holdingLine EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]
    /\ holdingBlock' = [holdingBlock EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]

Restart(t) ==
    /\ t \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lineLock, blockOcc, holdingLine, holdingBlock>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Trains, l \in Lines : AcquireLine(t, l)
    \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : EnterBlock(t, b)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : LeaveBlock(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : ReleaseLine(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Crash(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Restart(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OccupancyConsistent ==
    /\ \A b \in Blocks : blockOcc[b] # NONE => holdingBlock[blockOcc[b]] = b

CONSTANTS Trains = {10, 20} Lines = {0, 1} Blocks = {1, 2, 3}
INIT Init
NEXT Next

nl:
A subway signalling system protects track using a two-level, coarse-then-fine locking discipline. Each block of track belongs to a line; the line is the coarse lock and each block is a fine lock. A train must first acquire its target block's line lock, and only then may it enter and occupy the block itself. The system keeps two records: for each block, which train occupies it, and for each train, which block it currently holds. A train may leave its block, releasing the block record, and may release its line lock once it holds no block. Any train may crash silently at any moment; a silent crash removes the train and, to keep the railway running, automatically releases whatever line lock and block it was holding. A crashed train may later restart. The essential safety requirement is that the per-block and per-train occupancy records always agree with each other, so a block is never recorded as occupied by one train while a different train believes it holds that block, i.e. no block is double-allocated.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the per-block occupancy record and the per-train holding record are always mutually consistent, so no track block is ever allocated to two trains at once.

A smart-home door-lock network grants exclusive time slots to requesters who want temporary access. A set of lock controllers votes on which requester should get each slot. Votes are sent as messages that collect in a shared pool and may be counted in any order, not in the order they were sent. Each slot is either free or granted; initially every slot is free and unowned. A slot is granted to a requester only when it is still free and a quorum of controller votes backs that requester for that slot; granting moves the slot from the free set into the granted set and records the owning requester. A granted slot may later be released, which returns it to the free set, clears its owner, and discards any votes that referred to it so the slot can be contested again. Stray votes may also be garbage-collected from the pool at any time. The system must never hand the same slot to two different requesters, which it guarantees by keeping the free and granted sets disjoint and keeping the owner record in step with the granted set.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the free and granted slot sets are always disjoint, and a slot has a recorded owner exactly when it is in the granted set, so no slot is double-allocated.

---- MODULE W4Od5m4p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences
CONSTANTS Players, Seats, MaxCap
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES queue, seatOwner, playerSeat, cap, activeSeats
vars == <<queue, seatOwner, playerSeat, cap, activeSeats>>

InQueue(p) == \E i \in 1..Len(queue) : queue[i] = p

Init ==
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ seatOwner = [s \in Seats |-> NONE]
    /\ playerSeat = [p \in Players |-> NONE]
    /\ cap = 1
    /\ activeSeats = Seats

Enqueue(p) ==
    /\ playerSeat[p] = NONE
    /\ ~InQueue(p)
    /\ Len(queue) < cap
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, p)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seatOwner, playerSeat, cap, activeSeats>>

Assign(s) ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ s \in activeSeats
    /\ seatOwner[s] = NONE
    /\ LET p == Head(queue) IN
        /\ seatOwner' = [seatOwner EXCEPT ![s] = p]
        /\ playerSeat' = [playerSeat EXCEPT ![p] = s]
        /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, activeSeats>>

Leave(p) ==
    /\ playerSeat[p] # NONE
    /\ seatOwner' = [seatOwner EXCEPT ![playerSeat[p]] = NONE]
    /\ playerSeat' = [playerSeat EXCEPT ![p] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, cap, activeSeats>>

ChangeCap ==
    /\ \E c \in 1..MaxCap : cap' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, seatOwner, playerSeat, activeSeats>>

ActivateSeat(s) ==
    /\ s \notin activeSeats
    /\ activeSeats' = activeSeats \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, seatOwner, playerSeat, cap>>

DeactivateSeat(s) ==
    /\ s \in activeSeats
    /\ seatOwner[s] = NONE
    /\ activeSeats' = activeSeats \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, seatOwner, playerSeat, cap>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Players : Enqueue(p)
    \/ \E s \in Seats : Assign(s)
    \/ \E p \in Players : Leave(p)
    \/ ChangeCap
    \/ \E s \in Seats : ActivateSeat(s)
    \/ \E s \in Seats : DeactivateSeat(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
    /\ \A p \in Players : playerSeat[p] # NONE => seatOwner[playerSeat[p]] = p
    /\ \A s \in Seats : seatOwner[s] # NONE =>
            (playerSeat[seatOwner[s]] = s /\ s \in activeSeats)
====

CONSTANTS Players = {p1, p2} Seats = {s1, s2} MaxCap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker seats waiting players into lobby seats. Players who want a match join a bounded waiting queue; when the queue is already at its current capacity the matchmaker applies backpressure and refuses to admit the player. The queue capacity is not fixed: an operator may change it at runtime within an allowed range. The set of active seats can also change at runtime as lobbies open and close, but a seat may only be deactivated while it is empty. The matchmaker keeps two records: for each seat, which player occupies it, and for each player, which seat they hold. When the player at the head of the queue is seated, the matchmaker picks an active empty seat, links the seat to the player and the player to the seat, and removes the player from the queue. A seated player may later leave, clearing both links. The two records must always agree, and every occupied seat must be an active seat, so no seat is ever handed to two players at once.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the per-seat and per-player occupancy records always agree, and every occupied seat is active, so no seat is double-allocated.

---- MODULE W4Od4m7p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Stages, Total, MaxOverride

VARIABLES buf, inflight, moving, reg, overrides
vars == <<buf, inflight, moving, reg, overrides>>

RECURSIVE SumF(_)
SumF(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
           ELSE LET x == CHOOSE e \in S : TRUE IN buf[x] + SumF(S \ {x})


Init ==
    /\ buf = [i \in Stages |-> IF i = 1 THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ inflight = 0
    /\ moving = 0
    /\ reg = 0
    /\ overrides = 0

Pick(i) ==
    /\ inflight = 0
    /\ (i + 1) \in Stages
    /\ buf[i] > 0
    /\ buf' = [buf EXCEPT ![i] = @ - 1]
    /\ inflight' = 1
    /\ moving' = i
    /\ reg' = buf[i + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED overrides

CasCommit ==
    /\ inflight = 1
    /\ reg = buf[moving + 1]
    /\ buf' = [buf EXCEPT ![moving + 1] = @ + 1]
    /\ inflight' = 0
    /\ moving' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, overrides>>

CasRetry ==
    /\ inflight = 1
    /\ reg # buf[moving + 1]
    /\ reg' = buf[moving + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<buf, inflight, moving, overrides>>

AdminForce ==
    /\ inflight = 1
    /\ overrides < MaxOverride
    /\ buf' = [buf EXCEPT ![moving + 1] = @ + 1]
    /\ inflight' = 0
    /\ moving' = 0
    /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED reg

Recycle ==
    /\ buf[3] > 0
    /\ buf' = [buf EXCEPT ![3] = @ - 1, ![1] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inflight, moving, reg, overrides>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Stages : Pick(i)
    \/ CasCommit
    \/ CasRetry
    \/ AdminForce
    \/ Recycle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

Conserved == SumF(Stages) + inflight = Total
====

CONSTANTS Stages = {1, 2, 3} Total = 2 MaxOverride = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conserved
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line moves a fixed population of car tokens through a sequence of stages: entry, washing, and drying/exit. Tokens are never created or destroyed; they only move forward one stage at a time, and tokens that reach the last stage are recycled back to the first so the line keeps running. Moving a token uses a compare-and-swap discipline. A worker first picks a token out of a source stage, holding it in a single in-flight slot and snapshotting the destination stage's count into a shared register. It then attempts to commit the token into the next stage: the commit succeeds only if the register still matches the destination count, in which case the destination count is incremented and the in-flight slot is emptied. If the destination count has changed since the snapshot, the worker re-snapshots and retries. A privileged administrator may force a commit that bypasses the compare-and-swap check entirely, up to a bounded number of times. Throughout all of this the total number of tokens, counting those sitting in stages plus the one possibly in flight, must remain constant.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the sum of tokens across all stages plus any in-flight token always equals the fixed total, so no token is ever created or destroyed.

A hospital runs two independent operating-room scheduling instances that draw from one shared pool of operating-room time slots. A slot may be booked by either instance, but a booking is only committed once a quorum of schedulers votes for that instance taking that slot. Votes are messages naming a voter, a slot, and the instance; they accumulate until a quorum is reached. Booking a slot requires the slot to still be free in the shared pool; committing the booking removes the slot from the free pool, records a booking pairing the slot with the owning instance, credits the instance's held count, and clears the votes that referred to that slot. A booking may later be cancelled, which returns the slot to the free pool, decrements the instance's held count, and again clears any stale votes for the slot. Because two independent instances contend for the same pool, the crucial requirement is that a slot is never booked by two different instances: every booking record for a given slot must name the same instance.

SAFETY PROPERTY: for any two booking records referring to the same slot, they name the same instance, so no operating-room slot is ever allocated to two instances at once.

---- MODULE W4Od9m6p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Feeders, Instances, MaxTime, LeaseDur
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES lease, expiry, now, permit, shedBy
vars == <<lease, expiry, now, permit, shedBy>>

Init ==
    /\ lease = [f \in Feeders |-> NONE]
    /\ expiry = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
    /\ now = 0
    /\ permit = [f \in Feeders |-> 1]
    /\ shedBy = [f \in Feeders |-> NONE]

Acquire(i, f) ==
    /\ lease[f] = NONE
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![f] = i]
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![f] = now + LeaseDur]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<now, permit, shedBy>>

Expire(f) ==
    /\ lease[f] # NONE
    /\ expiry[f] <= now
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![f] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<expiry, now, permit, shedBy>>

Renew(i, f) ==
    /\ lease[f] = i
    /\ expiry[f] > now
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![f] = now + LeaseDur]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, now, permit, shedBy>>

Tick ==
    /\ now < MaxTime
    /\ now' = now + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, expiry, permit, shedBy>>

Shed(i, f) ==
    /\ lease[f] = i
    /\ expiry[f] > now
    /\ permit[f] > 0
    /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1]
    /\ shedBy' = [shedBy EXCEPT ![f] = i]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, expiry, now>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances, f \in Feeders : Acquire(i, f)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Expire(f)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, f \in Feeders : Renew(i, f)
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E i \in Instances, f \in Feeders : Shed(i, f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleShed == \A f \in Feeders : permit[f] >= 0
====

CONSTANTS Feeders = {f1, f2} Instances = {A, B} MaxTime = 2 LeaseDur = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleShed
nl:
A power-grid load shedder uses lease-based ownership over a shared pool of feeders, contended by two independent shedding instances. To gain the right to act on a feeder, an instance acquires a lease that is stamped with an expiry time computed from the current clock. A global clock ticks forward. A lease that has reached or passed its expiry time is considered expired and may be cleared, after which either instance may acquire the feeder again. A lease holder may renew its still-valid lease, pushing the expiry further out. The irreversible action in this system is shedding a feeder, which physically disconnects load and cannot be undone; each feeder carries exactly one shed permit. An instance may shed a feeder only while it holds a currently valid, unexpired lease on that feeder and the feeder's permit is still available, and doing so consumes the permit. Because there is only one permit per feeder, the irreversible shed can happen at most once, and the permit count for a feeder must never drop below zero.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every feeder's shed-permit count is always greater than or equal to zero, so the irreversible shed action is performed at most once per feeder.

EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Runways, Aircraft
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES used, snap, want, onRunway, cap
vars == <<used, snap, want, onRunway, cap>>

Init ==
    /\ used = [r \in Runways |-> 0]
    /\ snap = [a \in Aircraft |-> 0]
    /\ want = [a \in Aircraft |-> NONE]
    /\ onRunway = [a \in Aircraft |-> NONE]
    /\ cap = [r \in Runways |-> 1]

Read(a, r) ==
    /\ want[a] = NONE
    /\ onRunway[a] = NONE
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![a] = r]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![a] = used[r]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<used, onRunway, cap>>

CommitAcquire(a, r) ==
    /\ want[a] = r
    /\ used[r] = snap[a]
    /\ used[r] < cap[r]
    /\ used' = [used EXCEPT ![r] = 1]
    /\ onRunway' = [onRunway EXCEPT ![a] = r]
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![a] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, cap>>

RetryStale(a, r) ==
    /\ want[a] = r
    /\ used[r] # snap[a]
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![a] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<used, snap, onRunway, cap>>

Depart(a) ==
    /\ onRunway[a] # NONE
    /\ used' = [used EXCEPT ![onRunway[a]] = 0]
    /\ onRunway' = [onRunway EXCEPT ![a] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, want, cap>>

Activate(r) ==
    /\ cap[r] = 0
    /\ cap' = [cap EXCEPT ![r] = 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<used, snap, want, onRunway>>

Deactivate(r) ==
    /\ cap[r] = 1
    /\ used[r] = 0
    /\ cap' = [cap EXCEPT ![r] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<used, snap, want, onRunway>>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft, r \in Runways : Read(a, r)
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft, r \in Runways : CommitAcquire(a, r)
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft, r \in Runways : RetryStale(a, r)
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft : Depart(a)
    \/ \E r \in Runways : Activate(r)
    \/ \E r \in Runways : Deactivate(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

    \A r \in Runways : Cardinality({a \in Aircraft : onRunway[a] = r}) <= cap[r]
====

CONSTANTS Runways = {rw1, rw2} Aircraft = {ac1, ac2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator grants aircraft exclusive use of runways using optimistic locking with retry. Each runway has a shared usage register that is zero when the runway is free and one when it is in use, and each runway has a runtime capacity that is one while the runway is active and zero while it is deactivated. To claim a runway an aircraft first reads and snapshots the runway's usage register, recording which runway it is attempting. It then tries to commit: the commit succeeds only if the usage register still equals the snapshot and the runway's capacity still leaves room, in which case the register is set to in-use and the aircraft is recorded as being on that runway. If the register has changed since the snapshot, the optimistic attempt is stale and the aircraft abandons it to retry later. An aircraft on a runway may depart, freeing the register. Controllers may activate an inactive runway, and may deactivate a runway only while it is unused, changing capacity at runtime. The safety requirement is that the number of aircraft simultaneously on any runway never exceeds that runway's current capacity, giving mutual exclusion of the runway.

SAFETY PROPERTY: for every runway, the number of aircraft recorded as being on it is at most that runway's current capacity, so at most one aircraft ever uses an active runway at a time.

EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Courses, Students, Cap, MaxEpoch
Capacity(c) == Cap

VARIABLES occupied, freeSeats, enrolled, pool, epoch
vars == <<occupied, freeSeats, enrolled, pool, epoch>>

    /\ occupied = [c \in Courses |-> 0]
    /\ freeSeats = [c \in Courses |-> Cap]
    /\ enrolled = [c \in Courses |-> {}]
    /\ pool = {}
    /\ epoch = 0

Request(s, c, k) ==
    /\ k \in {"enroll", "drop"}
    /\ [student |-> s, course |-> c, kind |-> k] \notin pool
    /\ pool' = pool \cup {[student |-> s, course |-> c, kind |-> k]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, freeSeats, enrolled, epoch>>

ApplyEnroll(m) ==
    /\ m \in pool
    /\ m.kind = "enroll"
    /\ m.student \notin enrolled[m.course]
    /\ freeSeats[m.course] > 0
    /\ occupied' = [occupied EXCEPT ![m.course] = @ + 1]
    /\ freeSeats' = [freeSeats EXCEPT ![m.course] = @ - 1]
    /\ enrolled' = [enrolled EXCEPT ![m.course] = @ \cup {m.student}]
    /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

ApplyDrop(m) ==
    /\ m \in pool
    /\ m.kind = "drop"
    /\ m.student \in enrolled[m.course]
    /\ occupied' = [occupied EXCEPT ![m.course] = @ - 1]
    /\ freeSeats' = [freeSeats EXCEPT ![m.course] = @ + 1]
    /\ enrolled' = [enrolled EXCEPT ![m.course] = @ \ {m.student}]
    /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ pool' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, freeSeats, enrolled>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Students, c \in Courses, k \in {"enroll", "drop"} : Request(s, c, k)
    \/ \E m \in pool : ApplyEnroll(m)
    \/ \E m \in pool : ApplyDrop(m)
    \/ Reconfigure

    \A c \in Courses : occupied[c] + freeSeats[c] = Capacity(c)
====

CONSTANTS Courses = {cs1, cs2} Students = {st1, st2} Cap = 2 MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SeatsConserved
nl:
A university course-registration system manages a fixed number of seats per course; every seat is either occupied by an enrolled student or free, and seats are never created or destroyed. Students submit enroll and drop requests as messages that collect in a shared pool and may be processed in any order, not in the order submitted. Applying an enroll request for a student who is not already enrolled in that course, while a free seat exists, moves one seat from free to occupied and records the student's enrollment. Applying a drop request for a currently enrolled student moves one seat back from occupied to free and removes the enrollment. Periodically the registrar performs a numbered reconfiguration that bumps a registration epoch and discards all pending requests still sitting in the pool, since they belong to the old configuration. Existing enrollments are preserved across reconfigurations. Regardless of how requests are interleaved or how often the system reconfigures, each course's occupied plus free seat count must always equal that course's fixed capacity.

SAFETY PROPERTY: for every course, the number of occupied seats plus the number of free seats always equals the course's fixed capacity, so no seat is ever created or destroyed.

vars == <<inSector, permission, request, epoch>>

A bank's interbank settlement batch allocates settlement slots to member banks by quorum vote. Each slot carries exactly one allocation permit. Voters cast messages naming a voter, a slot, and a candidate bank; the messages accumulate until a quorum backs a particular bank for a particular slot. Voters may be slow, casting their votes late, but none ever fails or drops out, so a quorum can always eventually form. A hospital operating-room scheduler is driven by two independent scheduling instances that share one pool of operating rooms. Each room has an availability flag that is one when the room is free and zero when it is occupied, plus a record of which instance currently occupies it. An instance first requests a room, adding it to its private wish list. It may then acquire a room from its wish list only while that room's availability flag is one; acquiring flips the flag to zero, records the occupying instance, and removes the room from the wish list.     /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, served>>

    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inventory, capacity, served>>

    /\ inventory' = [inventory EXCEPT ![m] = @ - 1]
    /\ served' = served \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, capacity>>

    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, inventory, served>>

nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler feeds surgery requests through a bounded work queue into a set of operating-room slots. Requests are appended to the queue; when the queue is already full the scheduler applies backpressure and refuses the request. Every slot is either in the free set or the allocated set, and these two sets always partition all slots; each allocated slot records the surgery that owns it while free slots have no owner. Assigning takes the request at the head of the queue and, if some slot is free, moves that slot from the free set into the allocated set, records the surgery as its owner, and removes the request from the queue. A slot may be released, returning it to the free set and clearing its owner. A privileged administrator may also force-release an allocated slot, bypassing the normal flow, but only a bounded number of such overrides are allowed. The essential requirement is that the free and allocated sets never overlap and that a slot has an owner exactly when it is allocated, so no operating-room slot is ever handed out twice.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the free and allocated slot sets are always disjoint and partition all slots, and a slot has a recorded owner exactly when it is allocated, so no slot is double-allocated.

vars == <<rec, committed, snapRec, snapBase, crashed, epoch>>

SumDelta(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
               ELSE LET x == CHOOSE e \in S : TRUE IN DELTA[x] + SumDelta(S \ {x})

Init ==
    /\ rec = 0
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ snapRec = [u \in Updaters |-> NONE]
    /\ snapBase = [u \in Updaters |-> {}]
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ epoch = 0

Start(u) ==
    /\ snapRec[u] = NONE
    /\ u \notin committed
    /\ u \notin crashed
    /\ snapRec' = [snapRec EXCEPT ![u] = rec]
    /\ snapBase' = [snapBase EXCEPT ![u] = committed]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, committed, crashed, epoch>>

Commit(u) ==
    /\ snapRec[u] # NONE
    /\ u \notin committed
    /\ u \notin crashed
    /\ snapBase[u] = committed
    /\ rec' = snapRec[u] + DELTA[u]
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {u}
    /\ snapRec' = [snapRec EXCEPT ![u] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snapBase, crashed, epoch>>

Abort(u) ==
    /\ snapRec[u] # NONE
    /\ u \notin committed
    /\ snapBase[u] # committed
    /\ snapRec' = [snapRec EXCEPT ![u] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, committed, snapBase, crashed, epoch>>

Crash(u) ==
    /\ u \notin crashed
    /\ Cardinality(crashed) < Cardinality(Updaters) - 1
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {u}
    /\ snapRec' = [snapRec EXCEPT ![u] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, committed, snapBase, epoch>>

Restart(u) ==
    /\ u \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {u}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, committed, snapRec, snapBase, epoch>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ rec' = 0
    /\ committed' = {}
    /\ snapRec' = [u \in Updaters |-> NONE]
    /\ snapBase' = [u \in Updaters |-> {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

Next ==
    \/ \E u \in Updaters : Start(u)
    \/ \E u \in Updaters : Commit(u)
    \/ \E u \in Updaters : Abort(u)
    \/ \E u \in Updaters : Crash(u)
    \/ \E u \in Updaters : Restart(u)
    \/ Reconfigure

nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker maintains a shared readiness record that several updater clients modify concurrently. Each updater contributes a fixed readiness delta and, to modify the record safely, performs a read-modify-write. It first starts an update by snapshotting the current record value and snapshotting the set of updaters that have already been committed. Committing an update writes the snapshotted value plus the updater's delta back into the shared record. To prevent a lost update, a commit is allowed only if the committed set has not changed since the updater took its snapshot; if it has changed, the update is stale and is aborted so it can be retried. Any updater may crash silently at any time, which drops whatever update it had in flight without notice; the system always keeps at least one updater alive, and a crashed updater may later restart. Periodically the lobby reconfigures to a new epoch, which starts a fresh round: the shared record is reset to zero and no updater is considered committed. The shared record must always equal the sum of the deltas of exactly the currently committed updaters, so no committed update is ever lost or double-applied.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared readiness record always equals the sum of the deltas of the currently committed updaters, so no committed update is ever lost.
